data.name: Lenin - The Lion
data.detailed_description:
-- Developer's Note --

About the Portuguese (BR) version: the Portuguese language can be accessed by changing the menu language on the Steam App / a versão em português pode ser acessada alterando o idioma padrão da Steam e efetuando a atualização por download dos dados do jogo.

This game was individually developed by me, Lornyon. In the last few weeks I've solved all the bugs I found in the game and tried to fix as much writing problems as possible. But in any case, I ask for community collaboration and understanding if you still encounter such problems. In addition, I will be constantly looking to solve anything that might interrupt your enjoyment, and if you encounter any problems in the game, please let me know and I will fix it as soon as possible. Thanks.

                


Lenin is an albino lion, the only one of his kind, and because of that he feels insecure and constantly discouraged. Worse, his mother does not understand why his son was born this way, and the whole village despises him and treats him cruelly. At school, he suffers bullying and can’t concentrate on class.

Now, hopeless about life, certain situations seem to awaken in Lenin something that is not of everyone’s reality, but only of his. Something he will discover to be part of something else.
Besides, Lenin will find other animals species , which may help him to understand himself.
However, things are getting dangerous and Lenin needs to take care with his actions (your actions).

Traveling between daily life and a strange place, Lenin will have to face his inner fears and enemies – and often, the outer ones as well.



Lenin - The Lion is like a typical aerial-view RPGs of the SNES or Gameboy Color classics. The difference here is given by some criteria:

  • There are no battles or levels: all actions taken by the player are through conversations with NPC's, puzzles and varied options.
  • There is always more than one choice to proceed: yes, though many games work with "moral choices", in Lenin - The Lion choices don't change the character profile, but how is the unfolding of the main plot. With this in mind, don't expect multiple paths inside of the same part of the story. Your actions change the FUTURE scenes of the game, as well the endings of each area, unlocking new conversations with NPC's and different endings for the game as a whole.



  • A teenager's world and his struggles.
  • No battle systems or levels.
  • Lenin’s backpack is his menu. Losing it means not having access to the menu.
  • Items and puzzles are crucial in the interactions between Lenin and the others.
  • Choices determine the different endings of the game.
  • Original art / soundtrack.
  • Anthropomorphized characters.
  • A cute and unique main character ❤

CONTROLS:

MOVE: ARROWS & W-A-S-D
MENU: RIGHT MOUSE BUTTON TO ENTER, MOVE THE MOUSE TO NAVIGATE
CONFIRM: Z / ENTER / MOUSE LEFT BUTTON
CANCEL: X / ESC
FAST FOWARD TEXT: PAGE DOWN (PG DN)

JOYSTICKS ARE ONLY PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. YOU HAVE TO USE THE MOUSE IN ORDER TO ACCESS THE MENU.

FOR FULLSCREEN PRESS F4

If you are experiencing any lag in-game:

- Go the website of your graphics card manufacture (NVIDIA, AMD, etc.) and download & install the latest driver for your graphics card.
Make sure that the driver supports OpenGL.

data.short_description: Lenin – The Lion is a Puzzle RPG game about overcoming fears. Walk into chaos and find the claws of loneliness or carefully build your path and find the benefits of understanding and acceptance.

reviews.review:
Lenin - The Lion is an emotionally engaging indie adventure that combines psychological storytelling, exploration, and meaningful decision-making into a distinctive role-playing experience. Developed and published by Lornyon, the game follows an albino lion struggling with loneliness, bullying, depression, and the painful experience of being different. Beneath its charming pixel-art presentation lies a surprisingly mature narrative that explores self-acceptance, emotional vulnerability, and the consequences of personal choices. Rather than emphasizing traditional RPG combat, the adventure focuses on character development and storytelling, offering a thoughtful experience for players who appreciate games with deeper emotional themes.

The story introduces Lenin as a young lion whose unusual white appearance makes him a target of discrimination and ridicule. His daily life is filled with difficulties, including bullying at school and a complicated relationship with his mother, who struggles to understand his feelings. These circumstances gradually affect his confidence and emotional well-being, creating a sympathetic protagonist whose greatest challenges are psychological rather than physical. Following a particularly troubling experience, Lenin encounters a mysterious forest that leads him into a surreal journey through unfamiliar environments. This transition between reality and fantasy becomes an effective storytelling device, allowing the adventure to explore complicated emotions through imaginative encounters and symbolic situations.

One of the game's strongest qualities is its unconventional approach to RPG mechanics. Instead of fighting enemies, earning experience points, or improving combat statistics, players progress through exploration, conversations, puzzles, and consequential decisions. This design encourages careful observation and thoughtful interaction with the surrounding world. The absence of conventional battles complements the narrative's psychological focus, ensuring that emotional struggles remain central to the experience. Although players expecting elaborate combat systems may find the mechanics limited, the alternative approach gives the adventure a refreshing identity.

Decision-making plays an important role throughout the journey. Conversations and actions can influence future events, relationships, and narrative outcomes, encouraging players to consider the consequences of their behavior. Multiple endings provide opportunities to explore alternative storylines, while the single-save system makes individual decisions feel particularly significant. This restriction strengthens the sense of responsibility associated with each choice, although it can become frustrating when players wish to experiment with different possibilities without restarting their progress.

Another distinctive feature is the backpack inventory system. Rather than functioning as an ordinary menu, Lenin's backpack exists as an important possession within the game world. Losing it temporarily prevents access to stored belongings and restricts the collection of additional items. This mechanic introduces an unusual connection between gameplay functionality and narrative circumstances. While occasionally inconvenient, it demonstrates the developer's creativity and willingness to challenge familiar adventure-game conventions.

Exploration takes players through four unusual fantasy lands containing distinctive environments, memorable encounters, and various puzzles. These locations provide visual diversity while reflecting different aspects of the protagonist's emotional journey. Environmental challenges and minigames help maintain engagement between major story developments, although their complexity generally remains approachable. The emphasis on discovery makes the experience particularly suitable for players who enjoy investigating environments and uncovering narrative details rather than overcoming demanding mechanical challenges.

Visually, the game benefits from charming pixel artwork, expressive characters, and imaginative environmental design. Its colorful appearance contrasts effectively with the darker psychological subjects explored throughout the story. Specially illustrated scenes enhance important narrative moments, providing additional personality and emotional impact. Although the graphics are technically modest, their artistic consistency creates a recognizable atmosphere that supports the game's storytelling ambitions.

The soundtrack further strengthens the presentation through more than thirty musical compositions. Different tracks complement the changing environments and emotional circumstances, helping establish the appropriate atmosphere throughout the adventure. A particularly enjoyable feature is the portable music player, which allows Lenin to listen to collectible CDs discovered during exploration. This small addition provides another incentive to investigate the world while integrating the soundtrack naturally into the gameplay.

The narrative's exploration of bullying, depression, insecurity, and social isolation represents its greatest strength. These subjects are treated as fundamental elements of Lenin's experiences rather than superficial background details. The fantasy setting allows difficult emotions to be represented symbolically, encouraging empathy and reflection. However, the story's serious subject matter may feel uncomfortable for some players, while its occasional reliance on symbolism might not appeal to those who prefer straightforward storytelling.

Despite its creative qualities, the experience has noticeable limitations. The lack of combat and conventional progression reduces mechanical variety, while the restrictive saving system can discourage experimentation. Certain puzzles may interrupt the narrative's momentum, and repeated playthroughs can involve revisiting familiar conversations and environments. Nevertheless, these weaknesses are balanced by the game's distinctive personality, branching narrative, and commitment to emotionally meaningful storytelling.

Regarding Steam Deck compatibility, Lenin - The Lion does not have a confirmed official Verified or Playable classification based on the available information. Its modest technical requirements and two-dimensional presentation suggest that running it through Proton may be feasible, but functionality remains unverified. Controller configuration, text readability, and potential compatibility issues should be considered before playing on Valve's handheld.

Overall, Lenin - The Lion delivers a memorable psychological adventure that values empathy, personal growth, and meaningful choices over traditional RPG complexity. Its imaginative environments, charming artwork, atmospheric music, and unconventional mechanics create an experience with considerable emotional appeal. While its limited gameplay variety and restrictive saving system prevent it from achieving its full potential, the thoughtful narrative makes it worthwhile for players seeking a reflective, story-driven journey.

A touching and imaginative adventure with strong emotional storytelling, distinctive mechanics, and memorable artistic direction. Recommended for players who appreciate narrative-focused RPGs and psychological themes.

Rating: 8/10
